channel.title: Midnight blog - en - Last 7 days
channel.description: 记录软件从需求、架构设计、开发、测试到发布、运维与持续改进的工程实践，讨论具体约束、方案取舍和验证方法。AI 是工具链的一部分。 | Language: en | Range: Last 7 days

item.title: A Dependency Cache Hit Is Not Proof of a Valid Release
item.description: Treat dependency caches as disposable acceleration inputs while preserving lockfile checks and artifact provenance.

item.title: Two Deployments Overlap: Should the Lock Follow the Branch or the Environment?
item.description: Coordinate deployment writers around the target environment and verify final state after cancellation or overlapping runs.

item.title: If a Workflow Does Not Pass a Token, Can an Action Still Access It?
item.description: Limit GITHUB_TOKEN permissions per job and inspect implicit token access before trusting build and publication boundaries.

item.title: Both Saves Succeeded: Why Did One Editor Lose Their Changes?
item.description: Combine strong ETags with atomic version checks and a conflict workflow that preserves unsaved edits.

item.title: Can a Timed-Out Request Be Retried? Define the Business Idempotency Boundary
item.description: Define stable intent and durable deduplication before retrying an order whose outcome is unknown.

item.title: Search Results Went Backward: Cancellation Also Needs a State-Commit Guard
item.description: Combine request cancellation with identity guards on results and errors so older search responses cannot replace current intent.

item.title: Why Does no-cache Still Leave Cached Files?
item.description: Distinguish no-cache from no-store and private by checking validation and reuse across the actual delivery chain.

item.title: Does Replacing Order Numbers with UUIDs Prevent Unauthorized Access?
item.description: Keep object-level authorization independent of UUID guessability across downloads and asynchronous results.

item.title: Users Say They Would Use It: Ask About the Last Real Task First
item.description: Use recent task evidence to test product assumptions without confusing polite agreement with demand.

item.title: Database Slowness Restarts Every Pod: Is the Probe Asking the Wrong Question?
item.description: Match Kubernetes startup and readiness checks to their actions while reserving liveness restarts for appropriate failures.

item.title: The Node Is Idle: Why Is the Container Still Slow?
item.description: Separate Kubernetes requests from runtime limits and correlate container constraints with queues and business latency.

item.title: preStop Is Configured but Requests Still Fail: Budget the Whole Shutdown
item.description: Budget Kubernetes termination across hooks and in-flight work with observable completion rather than fixed sleep.

item.title: Why Should Customer Email Not Go Straight into OpenTelemetry Baggage?
item.description: Separate OpenTelemetry Baggage propagation from telemetry storage and keep sensitive data and authorization outside its trust.

item.title: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY Is Still Waiting: What Should a Release Check?
item.description: Plan PostgreSQL 18 concurrent index builds around transaction waits and validity rather than command completion alone.

item.title: A Query Is Slow: Check Row Estimates Before Adding an Index
item.description: Locate row-estimate errors and actual execution work in PostgreSQL 18 before choosing an index or query rewrite.

item.title: Both Transactions Committed: Why Did the Business Invariant Fail?
item.description: Protect PostgreSQL 18 business invariants with suitable concurrency controls and bounded whole-transaction retries.

item.title: The Backup Job Is Green: Why Does Recovery Still Fail?
item.description: Validate PostgreSQL 18 recovery through roles and restored business behavior instead of a successful backup-job status.

item.title: The Database Committed but the Notification Failed: Define the Handoff
item.description: Use a transactional outbox to make handoff recoverable while defining worker ownership and duplicate delivery handling.

item.title: The Key Was Deleted from Git: Why Is the Incident Not Over?
item.description: Verify replacement access and old-credential rejection across declared consumers instead of relying on source deletion.

item.title: A Server Fetches User URLs: Why Is Domain Validation Not Enough?
item.description: Bound server-side URL fetching through destination policy and redirect checks backed by controlled network egress.

item.title: A successful deployment is not a verified release
item.description: Separate source, artifacts, deployment, and user outcomes; rehearse rollback with data compatibility in mind.

item.title: “Support export” is not an acceptance criterion
item.description: Use an export workflow to separate acceptance scenarios, interface boundaries, and architecture decisions.

item.title: Green tests are not enough: design quality gates around failure paths
item.description: Prioritize logic, integration, end-to-end, security, and accessibility checks by the failures they detect.

item.title: Low CPU, failed users: connect service indicators to incident learning
item.description: Distinguish accepted requests from completed jobs, define indicator populations, and make incident actions verifiable.
